commit cc5d947918f6e8711c52aac568b55936d8458d42
Author: Jose Antonio Garrido <yeyochico@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat Sep 19 18:38:39 2026 +0200

    fix(web): give shiki's first call the time to compile its grammar
    
    shiki stops tokenizing a line after 500 ms and returns the rest of it as
    one uncoloured token. The first call in a language compiles its grammar
    inside that budget, and on a busy machine a heavy grammar overran it: the
    first code block on screen came out without colours, and the highlight
    test failed whenever the full suite ran alongside other work.
    
    The budget is now 2 s per line: still a guard against a pathological line,
    no longer tripped by the grammar's own start-up. With twelve busy loops on
    the CPU, a C++ block came back as a single plain run in 3 of 3 runs at
    500 ms and fully coloured in 3 of 3 at 2 s. The new test covers it.

diff --git a/apps/web/test/highlight.test.ts b/apps/web/test/highlight.test.ts
index bbc277e..8925513 100644

@@ -211,3 +211,12 @@ test('a shell line tells commands from their arguments', async () => {
 test('an unknown language is left plain', async () => {
   assert.equal(await highlight('whatever', 'not-a-language'), null);
 });
+
+test('the first block in a grammar shiki compiles on the spot is still coloured', async () => {
+  // C++ is not one of the languages the lighter highlighter covers, so it takes shiki's path,
+  // where the first call compiles the grammar inside the per-line time budget.
+  const out = await highlight('template <typename T> auto twice(const T& x) -> T { return x + x; } int main() { return twice(21); }', 'cpp');
+  assert.ok(out);
+  const styled = out.lines.flat().filter((run) => typeof run !== 'string');
+  assert.ok(styled.length >= 3, `expected keywords, types and literals coloured, got ${styled.length} runs`);
+});
